name: Dependent Pass and Long Term Social Visit Pass (LTSVP)

requirement_groups.name: Spouse/minor child of a work-pass holder

requirements.blocker_text: The sponsor must hold an Employment Pass (as of 1 June 2026, this includes Category III, previously excluded) or Residence Pass-Talent; covers the spouse and minor children.
requirements.fix_path: Wait until the sponsoring family member holds a qualifying Employment Pass category.

requirement_groups.name: Extended family of a Malaysian citizen or PR holder (LTSVP)

requirements.blocker_text: Covers spouses and parents of Malaysian citizens or Permanent Residents; sponsored by the Malaysian family member rather than an employer.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate or birth certificate proving the qualifying family relationship
Sponsor's valid Employment Pass, citizenship documentation, or PR status
Proof of financial support sufficient to avoid the dependent becoming a public charge

outcome.duration_length: Dependent Pass: tied to sponsor's Employment Pass validity; LTSVP: 6 months to 5 years

sources.title: MalaysiaVisas.com -- Malaysia Long Term Social Visit Pass - Complete Guide 2026, describing LTSVP eligibility and the Dependent Pass's Employment Pass-tied structure

Two structurally distinct passes are correctly modeled as separate OR-logic groups: the Dependent Pass (tied to an employer-sponsored Employment Pass, covering spouse and minor children only) and the LTSVP (sponsored by the Malaysian family member directly, covering a broader relationship set including parents, and usable regardless of the sponsor's own employment status). citizenship_after_months (24) reflects a route worth flagging clearly: per general PR/naturalisation research for this build, the marriage-to-citizen route requires the foreign spouse to first hold PR for a minimum period before naturalisation eligibility opens -- a 2025 reform reduced the minimum marriage duration for PR eligibility itself from 5 years to 3 years (see my_permanent_residence's spouse group for the primary citation), but the further step from PR to citizenship carries its own separate residency requirement documented in my_naturalisation; this figure should be treated as an approximation of the fastest realistic path rather than a fully independently traced chain. pr_after_months (36) reflects the same January 2025 reform reducing the marriage-duration requirement for PR eligibility from 5 to 3 years -- a genuine, dated liberalisation worth surfacing, contrasted with the general pattern of most other Malaysia routes in this build being tightened rather than loosened in 2025-2026 (Employment Pass thresholds, family-marriage-to-citizenship waiting periods in other countries documented elsewhere in this dataset).
